sketches.name: Common Bond
sketches.idea: A close-set TP monogram gives the parish initials a broad sheltering crossbar and an upward-cut return.
sketches.approach: Letter-led emblem: drawn contrast, a generous P counter, and restrained calligraphic terminals.
sketches.reason: Clearer initials, but the silhouette is less memorable and can resemble a conventional luxury monogram.

sketches.name: Response Medallion
sketches.idea: The P returns around the T to establish an enclosing circular emblem.
sketches.approach: In this initial construction the returning P also supplies the eastern edge of the open roundel.
sketches.reason: The strongest emblem silhouette. Its first lower junction was crowded; development separated the enclosing contour from the letter tails to improve reading.

sketches.name: Coupled Banner
sketches.idea: Two folded panels join around an upright interior seam.
sketches.approach: A textile-led emblem with no initials: paired panels, a shared crown, and a narrow central opening.
sketches.reason: A distinct non-letter alternative, but its closed mass can resemble a shield, book, or ceremonial badge and feels less welcoming.

developed.name: The Joined Roundel
developed.idea: An open enclosing roundel holds crafted T and P forms whose lower returns join its base.
developed.visible: An interrupted circle, a broad T, and a P with an open returning tail. The top opening and the P counter remain deliberate negative spaces.
developed.meaning: The enclosure proposes gathering and belonging; the lifted terminals give that held space a restrained outward response. The name initials anchor the emblem to this parish. This is a symbolic reading, not a literal depiction of worship.
construction: A 256-unit canvas contains an open outer roundel; its main body is approximately 18 units thick.
The T and P are independent original paths. Their lower tails overlap the ring at its base; the ring is not one continuous stroke made entirely from the initials.
V2 opened the counters and calmed the T terminal. V3 smooths only the P stem-to-tail junction; the earlier constructions remain preserved.
developed.risk: The ring and high-contrast TP can suggest a university, heritage institution, hotel, or luxury monogram. The returning P can also read as a decorative loop or lowercase e. Christian identity depends on the parish name and its separate RCCG relationship; it is not instantly explicit in the symbol.
developed.smallSize: Actual black/reverse tests: the silhouette persists at 16px, but TP reading and lower gaps are unreliable. 24px is marginal; 32px is the more credible symbol test, with 48px clearer. Complete lockups remain readable at 320px and 240px; those widths do not establish a print minimum.
developed.longevity: The one-color roundel and restrained letter contrast have durable precedents, but the heritage associations must be accepted deliberately. Its fine counter relationships need production proof before any small physical use.
developed.selectionReason: Selected over the bare monogram and coupled banner for its stronger silhouette and more coherent relationship between a held interior and a responding return. The developed ring improves clarity while giving up the initial sketch’s more literal one-contour integration.

type.family: Noto Serif Regular, outlined companion wordmark
type.edits: The companion name uses unchanged licensed Noto Serif glyph outlines with considered two-line spacing. The T/P symbol is original drawn artwork; it is not extracted from Noto Serif.
